stem:
Wafa looks at the diagram. Point $R$ lies on a straight line, and a right angle is to be built at $R$.

Which plan correctly constructs the $90^\circ$ angle at $R$?

options.text: Mark $X$ and $Y$ on the line with $XR = RY$, then draw the perpendicular bisector of $XY$ through $R$.
Mark any point $P$ above the line and join $P$ to $R$, without making $R$ the midpoint of a segment on the line.
First draw a $60^\circ$ angle at $R$ by an equilateral triangle, then halve it to get $30^\circ$.
Treat the finished right angle at $R$ as what chooses the equal points $X$ and $Y$ on the line.

teacher.key_rationale: Make R the midpoint of XY on the line, then the perpendicular bisector of XY is the 90° line at R. Skipping equal distances omits the midpoint step; building 60°/30° conflates another construction; saying the right angle chooses X and Y reverses the plan.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as a line with point R, equal points X and Y, and a perpendicular through R.
